title: Two optical moments limit the W1 opacity of Gaia20cdd for any dust column distribution
abstract: We derive a sharp transmission bound for dust with any column distribution and a common opacity law. For the published 2022 Gaia20cdd dip, W1/r opacity is at most 0.08204 at g/r opacity 1.788. The r and W1 bound alone is 0.12672. A uniform column plus clear holes attains the upper transmission bound. All 14 tested slow-mode ice models fail, including an optical tolerance box of 0.4 mag and a W1 depth raised by two errors. Nine of 12 silicate models and all 26 graphite models pass this necessary test. The least constant unocculted W1 emission needed to rescue a tested ice model is 0.81042 times the clear stellar W1 flux. Limits include a clear reference state, common surface weights, effective band opacities and nonsimultaneous depth summaries. The result does not exclude mixed ice or ice at another epoch. Code, proof, dual checks, aggregate results and exact source retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Sharp transmission bounds and optical tolerance tests under a common opacity law, a clear reference state and no added light.
